reuse.why: Weekend/holiday moves go through the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and RSchedule, but the daily-skip rule is not given a shared helper: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each write their own skip loop next to getNextDate's firstWeekdayOccurrence.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && frequency === daily' decision and the skip-weekend-occurrence filtering appear three times (shared getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange), and getDatesInRange re-codes the move-or-skip dispatch rather than sharing one per-occurrence adjust function.

placement.why: Holiday logic sits in shared/schedules correctly, but the daily-skip rule is spread across shared and server/schedules/app.ts, and schedule-template.ts only got the holidays argument, not the daily rule.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedules; the rule-utils data additions and four release notes are related to the steps.

maintainability.why: A future change to how an occurrence is adjusted (skip vs move vs holiday) must be applied in three places that already diverge (bounded take sizes, schedule-template not covered).

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement the daily weekend skip with isWeekendOrHoliday loops instead of going through a shared adjust/next-date helper; budget/schedule-template.ts calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend directly without the daily rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip filter is expressed three ways: firstWeekdayOccurrence in shared/schedules.ts, a bounded for-loop in getUpcomingDates, and a continue-in-loop with the move/skip dispatch in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a holidays parameter; getNextDate gained a daily-schedule branch (skipsWeekendDays in first lookup, reverse lookup and the move guard); getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template.ts decide skip-vs-move themselves.
